errors.evidence: For sparsity rates from 10% to 50%, the perplexity values are all clearly below the 10¹ (10) level, not just near it. They range from approximately 5 to 8.

errors.text_span: No bars are grouped or stacked
errors.evidence: The chart is a grouped bar chart, with bars grouped in pairs for each sparsity rate. The statement that bars are not grouped is incorrect and contradicts the latter part of the same sentence which mentions 'two adjacent bars'.
For sparsity rates from 10% to 50%, the perplexity values for both methods are visibly below the 10¹ line, not above it. The values appear to be in the range of approximately 5 to 8.

The orange bar for the “Per-Layer” method at 80% sparsity reaches a value very close to the 10³ line (1000), but it does not visibly exceed it. Describing it as exceeding 1000 is an inaccurate exaggeration.

errors.text_span: indicating a more severe degradation in performance under aggressive pruning
errors.evidence: This part of the sentence interprets the meaning of the perplexity metric ('degradation in performance') rather than strictly describing the visual information presented in the chart.

The bar for 'Per-Layer' at 80% sparsity has a value of approximately 900, very close to the 1000 mark on the logarithmic scale. While 'exceeds 600' is technically true, it is a significant understatement that misrepresents the magnitude of the value and the severity of the performance degradation compared to the 'Per-Output' method.
The y-axis does not have a labeled tick mark at 10⁰ (which is 1). The labeled ticks are at 10¹, 10², and 10³.
At low sparsity rates (10-50%), the bar values are not close to 10⁰ (which is 1). They are visibly in the range of approximately 4 to 8, which is closer to 10¹ than 10⁰.
At 70% sparsity, the blue 'Per-Output' bar is visibly well above 10¹ (which is 10), at a value of approximately 20.
At 70% sparsity, the orange 'Per-Layer' bar is not 'just above 10¹'. It is significantly higher, at a value of approximately 30-40.
At 80% sparsity, the orange 'Per-Layer' bar is close to but visibly below the 10³ (1000) line, not over it.
